transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

Grey smelly water left in the bottom after a cycle usually means the machine isn't draining completely, even if it seemed to finish. Since your kitchen sink was replaced recently, there are two main possibilities: either something has blocked the dishwasher's own filter or pump area, or the connection between the dishwasher hose and the new sink waste is restricted (for example, if the blanking plug inside the sink spigot wasn't removed). To narrow this down, please switch off and unplug the dishwasher. Remove the bottom rack, then twist and lift out the coarse filter in the base of the tub. Is it clogged with food or grease, and is the sump area underneath clear? If you can see a small pump cover under where the filter was, please also check if anything (like glass or a bone) is caught around the impeller.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

I checked the filter and it's clean, nothing stuck in it. The dishwasher drains fully at the end of a cycle. The dirty water seems to show up after I've drained the sink full of washing-up water, if that helps.

That pattern—water only appearing after the sink is drained—is a common sign of backflow. Since your sink was replaced recently, it is likely that the small plastic blanking plug inside the waste spigot (where the dishwasher hose connects) was left in place or not fully removed. This prevents water from flowing freely into the main drain and allows sink water to push back up into the dishwasher when you empty a full sink of washing-up water. Please check under the sink: if there is a plug inside that connection hole, remove it.

I looked under the sink. The drain hose just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, no loop or anything since the new sink went in. I'm not sure about a plug inside the spigot though, how would I tell? The sink does drain a little slow too.

To check for the blanking plug, shine a torch down into the hole in the waste spigot where your dishwasher hose connects. If you see a solid plastic disc or cap sealing it off from below, that is the plug and needs removing (usually by cutting it out with a utility knife). Is there a plug inside, or does the hole look open?

I haven't looked down the spigot with a torch yet, so I can't say about a plug. Is the lack of a high loop in the hose a problem though? It just goes straight from the dishwasher to the spigot along the cupboard floor.

Yes, the lack of a high loop is most likely part of the problem. Without it, gravity allows water from the sink to flow back down the dishwasher hose when the sink drains, which explains why you get smelly water in the machine after emptying the sink. This prevents sink water from flowing backwards into the machine even if the drain is slow.
Ok, so should I loop the hose up high and clip it? How high does it need to go?

Yes, creating a high loop is exactly what you need to do. Lift the hose up and secure it (using a clip or tie) so it reaches at least 60cm above the floor before it drops down into the sink waste. This height prevents gravity from pulling sink water back down into your dishwasher when the sink drains.
